name: Apple Fitness
description: Apple Fitness is the iPhone fitness hub for Activity rings, movement goals, trends, awards, workout history and activity sharing, with additional metrics from Apple Watch and compatible sensors. Apple Fitness+ adds a subscription library of guided workouts and meditations, personalized recommendations, training plans and live workout metrics.
agentUseSummary: Apple Fitness cannot be connected as a separate Relay account provider because Apple publishes no delegated Fitness or Fitness+ account API. Supported developer access to workout data uses HealthKit, and third-party workout scheduling uses WorkoutKit inside a native authorized app; those surfaces belong to the unresolved Apple Health device-local consent contract rather than a duplicate Apple Fitness connection.

blocked.label: Connect Apple Fitness
blocked.description: Apple publishes no OAuth, API-key, account API or remote MCP contract for a third party to connect the Fitness or Fitness+ account and library.

blocked.label: Read fitness activity
blocked.description: Activity rings, steps, distance, trends, awards, workouts, effort, heart rate, calories and shared activity are unavailable through a separate Fitness provider; supported workout-data access requires the Apple Health HealthKit contract.

blocked.label: Change goals or workouts
blocked.description: Agents cannot change Activity goals, log or delete completed workouts, manage sharing, schedule workouts or write fitness data without an approved native HealthKit and WorkoutKit implementation.

blocked.label: Control Apple Fitness+
blocked.description: Fitness+ subscriptions, recommendations, plans, trainer content, workout and meditation playback, awards and account history are not exposed through a supported third-party API.

blocked.label: Use private or credential-based access
blocked.description: Apple Account credentials, Fitness app automation, web scraping, private frameworks, database extraction and reverse-engineered service calls are never accepted.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No separate Apple Fitness action is enabled; supported native workout data and scheduling must use one approved Apple Health device-local connection instead.

runtimeSupport.description: No separate Apple Fitness tools are mounted because Apple exposes no Fitness account API and the supported HealthKit and WorkoutKit authority requires an approved native Apple Health bridge.

providerSetup.blocker: Apple Fitness and Fitness+ are interactive Apple apps and subscription services, not a delegated account platform. Apple exposes workout samples and health metrics through permissioned HealthKit, while WorkoutKit lets a third-party native iOS or watchOS app create, preview and schedule its own workout compositions with user authorization. Neither framework grants access to Fitness+ content, recommendations, subscriptions or an umbrella Fitness account. Relay's Apple Health iteration already records the unresolved native target, health-purpose, per-agent consent, third-party disclosure and data-governance decisions for this device-local authority.
providerSetup.nextAction: Do not request Apple Account credentials, show a separate Connect action or publish a duplicate Apple Fitness card. Keep Apple Fitness unavailable as a direct provider. If the Apple Health native contract is approved, include bounded workout reads and explicitly authorized WorkoutKit scheduling in that single device-local connection, with separate capabilities and permissions; only reconsider Fitness+ if Apple publishes a supported distributable account or content API.

evidence.supports: Apple describes the Fitness app as the interactive place to review Activity rings, steps, distance, trends and workouts, change goals and share activity with friends.
Apple describes Fitness+ as a paid workout and meditation content service with personalized recommendations, plans and device-provided real-time metrics inside the Fitness app.

WorkoutKit lets native iOS and watchOS apps create and preview their own workout compositions and, with permission, schedule them in the Workout app and Fitness app; it directs health-data access to HealthKit.
Apple models completed workouts as permission-protected HealthKit samples with activity, energy and distance data rather than a Fitness account API.
Apple's public health and fitness developer surfaces are HealthKit, Core Motion and WorkoutKit for native app experiences; Apple does not publish an umbrella Fitness or Fitness+ account API.

Apple restricts health and fitness data use, disclosure, data mining, inaccurate writes and storage, so the native Apple Health consent and governance boundary cannot be bypassed through a second provider identity.
